declaration.declared_before: any model score on this layer; sites and contexts are a deterministic function of the frozen first-stage cohort, so the selection cannot follow an observed effect
declaration.question: With every other position of one natural HSP fragment fixed, what twenty-way conditional probability does a causal model's canonical sequence score induce for the residue actually observed at one query position, and how does that observed log-probability compare with a training-only Profile and a training-only Markov description normalised over the very same twenty complete strings?
declaration.quantity: q_theta(a|rest) = softmax over AA20 of minus the summed native full-sequence NLL of the twenty complete single-substitution strings; the reported value is log q_theta of the observed residue
declaration.not_claimed: q_theta is a local conditional induced by a canonical score with the fragment held fixed, not a native next-token probability and not a recovered generative distribution; the fixed background itself carries family information and pretraining exposure of that family is unknown; the two contrasts are direct differences of observed log-scores, not a joint-model conditional increment; the pilot is descriptive only
declaration.scope: one new endpoint (conditional log-score) on the declared four pilot and sixty-four evaluation units of the first-stage cohort, each with its single fixed wild type and unchanged native fragments
declaration.out_of_scope: per-position rank-20 order, sampled or ancestral generation, pairwise drift, sequence design, re-ranking models by generative quality, and any comparison with the first-stage column-permutation family

parents.authority: the frozen cohort's own protocol snapshot supplies the roster, the pilot models, the precision policy, the score function and the token budget; this layer writes no second roster
inherits: wild types, native fragments, clusters and splits
parents.not_read: first-stage score documents, nulls and contrasts; this layer depends on the cohort inputs only, so it can be prepared and analysed without any first-stage model output
parents.natives: native strings, query maps and cluster splits are taken from the frozen queue; the 198MB corpus hit table is not re-read

selection.eligible_position: one query position carried by at least min_training_rows_with_site training representatives and at least min_heldout_rows_with_site held-out representatives of the unit's fixed wild type
selection.context: one held-out representative that carries the site's query position; its entire native string is held fixed and only the queried position is enumerated
selection.rng: one numpy default_rng(seed) consumed in ascending unit_id order; per unit one without-replacement draw of positions from the ascending eligible list, then per selected position in ascending order one without-replacement draw of contexts from row_id order; draws consume only uniform doubles through a partial Fisher-Yates pass, and nothing is redrawn after a result
selection.insufficient_support: a unit with no eligible query position is recorded with its support counts and reported explicitly; it is never silently dropped
selection.recorded: unit, wild type, row_id, cluster, native string, native index, query position, observed residue, the AA20 order, the available and selected site/context counts, and fitted baseline parameters; twenty-way baseline log-probabilities are derived only in memory after full manifest validation

baselines.fitting_rows: training-cluster representatives only; no held-out row and no nonrepresentative row is used
baselines.profile: per query-position residue counts plus 1/20 over AA20; because the twenty variants differ only at the queried position, the untouched terms are identical and cancel, leaving the position's twenty-way distribution
baselines.markov: AA20 start distribution and adjacent transitions of each continuous native training fragment plus 1/20; query-map gaps do not split the native chain
baselines.normalisation: each baseline is scored on the same twenty complete single-substitution strings as the model and normalised with the same log-sum-exp; the Markov description is the complete-string score, never the single forward transition alone
baselines.status: the observed logscore is a proper score on the common twenty-AA target; a positive lower bound of a nondegenerate paired simultaneous 95% interval supports the model outperforming that individual baseline on this target and support, once formal evaluation is complete; it does not establish full generative-distribution recovery, superiority over all joint lower-order controls, or a causal memory mechanism

statistics.aggregation: one value per site (mean of its contexts' observed log-scores), then one value per family (mean of its sites); families are equally weighted and a site's weight does not depend on its context count
statistics.columns: two contrasts per model, both direct differences of observed log-scores: <arm>|minus_profile and <arm>|minus_markov, so the inherited 33 arms give 66 labelled columns
statistics.primary: standardized maxT 95 over the 66 labelled columns, one new statistical family resampled by family
statistics.auxiliary: pointwise 95 from the same matrix of resampled family means
statistics.uniform_reference: log(1/20) nats is reported as a description of the twenty-way enumeration, not as a null
statistics.degeneracy: a column with zero empirical SE is labelled bootstrap degeneracy, never certainty of capability or equivalence
statistics.separation: this family is not the first-stage R1/R2/R3 families, nor the parent column-null family, and the three are never combined
statistics.formal_completion: no formal completion or significance until all 33 inherited arms cover every declared evaluation unit
